chunks: He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Baseer reported to me, saying: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Siyabah narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, who said:

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, said one day to his companions: "Be it known that a disease of the nations before you has crept into you, and that is envy. It does not shave off hair, but it shaves off religion. And one can be saved from it by restraining his hands, guarding his tongue, and not being one who slanders his believing brother."
And may God bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his pure family, and grant them abundant peace.

key_terms.الحسد: Hasad (envy) — wishing for the removal of a blessing from another person; considered a major spiritual disease in Islam
key_terms.حالق الدين: Shaver of religion — a metaphor indicating that envy destroys faith as completely as a razor shaves hair
key_terms.غمز: Ghamz — slandering, backbiting, or speaking ill of someone behind their back

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about envy (hasad) and its cure?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) warned his companions about envy (hasad), describing it as a spiritual disease inherited from past nations that destroys faith rather than outward appearance. He taught that the antidote to envy involves three practical measures: restraining one's actions (hands), controlling one's speech (tongue), and refraining from slandering fellow believers. This was delivered as a public sermon to the companions, using the vivid metaphor of "shaving" to contrast physical and spiritual harm.
